verdict.rationale: PayPal's agent toolkit and REST APIs expose broad merchant functionality (orders, invoices, subscriptions, refunds, disputes, catalog, shipment tracking) that maps to much of what's doable in the merchant UI, and sandbox/webhooks support full dev lifecycle. But agentic-commerce access is form-gated (not self-serve), Store Sync is scoped narrowly (US-only, physical goods only, no digital/subscription), and cart/checkout flows are reverse APIs merchants must host rather than full symmetric parity with dashboard actions — no evidence of comprehensive UI-to-API parity claim or audit. missing for 10: explicit UI-vs-API parity documentation, evidence covering account/dashboard-only settings (payouts, branding, dispute UI actions beyond accept_dispute_claim), and removal of form-gating/scope restrictions.
